children.description:
잎은 상록성이며 어긋나기이며, 옆으로 뻗은 가지에서는 두 줄로 배열되고 선형, 피침형이다. 뒷면에 연한 녹색 또는 회청색 줄이 있다. 배우체는 암수딴그루 또는 암수한그루로서 수술은 1개씩 또는 3-14개가 솔방울처럼 모여 달리며, 각 수 술에 3-8개의 소포자낭이 달린다. 배주는 보통 1개씩 육질 또는 흔적적인 심피 위에 달리며, 종자는 일부 또는 전부가 육질의 종자껍질로 싸여 있다.

분류학적 소견 최근에는 주목과를 독립 목으로 취급하지만, Engler 체계에서는 측백나무과와 함께 측백나무목으로 처리하고 있어 이 체계를 따랐다. 단, 본 도감에서는 주목과와 개비자나무과를 합쳐 부르는 Engler 체계와 달리, 주목과와 개비자나무과를 분리해서 제시하였다.

children.name: Lepidocupania arcuata  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Additional taxonomic analyses are required, especially with regard to material from the Loyalty Islands, which exhibits very peculiar indument compared to that from the main island of New Caledonia [Grande Terre]. Moreover, TURNER (1995) tentatively identified a specimen from Tonga (Parks 16317: L 0468503) as L. arcuata, which, if confirmed, would significantly expand the geographic range of this species.

children.name: Lepidocupania brackenridgei  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: The native range of this species is Solomon Is. to SW. Pacific. It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Lepidocupania concolor  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Distribution and ecology. – Lepidocupania concolor is endemic to Fiji, where it is known from the three main islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni (SMITH, 1985).

children.name: Lepidocupania fruticosa  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Based on our current knowledge on this species, additional taxonomic studies appear to be needed to clarify its circumscription. This should also include material currently assigned to L. subfalcata and L. tontoutensis (see below for additional details).

children.name: Lepidocupania glabra  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – This species has been assigned an IUCN risk of extinction status of “ Critically Endangered ” [CR] based on its narrow distribution and reduction in population size (IUCN, 2020).

children.name: Lepidocupania globosa  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – This species has been assigned an IUCN risk of extinction status of “ Vulnerable ” (IUCN, 2020). See note under L. pennelii.

children.name: Lepidocupania glomeriflora  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: The native range of this species is New Caledonia (incl. Îs. Loyauté). It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Lepidocupania gracilipes  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Distribution and ecology. – Lepidocupania gracilipes is endemic to Grande Terre, where it grows in gallery forest, continuous tall maquis (“ maquis paraforestier ”, see MCCOY et al., 1999 for details), and thickets on (rocky) serpentine terrain, and sometimes along streams on alluvium (TURNER, 1995). It seems to be restricted to serpentine, hyper-magnesium brown soils. The species has been recorded from sea level to 600 m.

children.name: Lepidocupania grandiflora  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – ADEMA (1991: 119) suggested a close affinity between this species and L. oedipoda based on vegetative characters. Their morphological similarity points toward the need for further analyses, especially focusing on collections from the Pouébo area.

children.name: Lepidocupania guillauminii  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Note. – While ADEMA (1991: 122) noted that the available material of this species is rather incomplete and that it resembles both L. concolor and L. samoensis, he recognized it as distinct based on several differences in the amount of indument and in features of the fruits.

children.name: Lepidocupania inoplea  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Cupaniopsis inoplea was described based on Balansa 3307. Original material at P is mounted on three sheets, two of which [P 00639140, P 00639141] bear the following note in Radlkofer’s hand: “ Cupaniopsis inoplaea m. Radlk. ” Here we designate the most complete and best-preserved of these two sheets [P 00639140] as the lectotype. children.name: Lepidocupania lepidota  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: The native range of this species is New Caledonia. It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Lepidocupania mouana  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Note. – Lepidocupania mouana was assigned an IUCN risk of extinction status of “ Endangered ” [EN] by JAFFRÉ et al. (1998).

children.name: Lepidocupania myrmoctona  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Cupaniopsis myrmoctona was described based on “ Labillardière (Hb. Webb, Hook., Deless.) ” (RADLKOFER, 1879 b: 588). ADEMA (1991: 140) designated material from G as the lectotype. A second step lectotypification is, however, required because the original material at G comprises three sheets originating from three different herbaria: Delessert [G 00019027], Moricand [G 00341590], and Ventenat [G 00341584]. children.name: Lepidocupania oedipoda  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Five syntypes were cited in the protologue of Cupaniopsis oedipoda: Balansa 153 p. p., 1441 and 2257, Baudouin 354 p. p. and Pancher s. n. ADEMA (1991: 146) designated Pancher s. n. as the lectotype. Original material of this collection at P is, however, mounted on four sheets, necessitating a second step lectotypification. children.name: Lepidocupania pennelii  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Cupaniopsis pennelii was described based on Pennel 403. Material of the collection at P is mounted on three sheets, but only one of them [P 00639152] bears the name of Guillaumin’s new species in his own hand, and we therefore regard it as the holotype. Lepidocupania pennelii is morphologically similar to L. globosa and L. rosea (the latter known only from the type specimen), whose ecological preferences and distributions are nearly the same. children.name: Lepidocupania rosea  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – See note under Lepidocupania pennelii.

children.name: Lepidocupania samoensis  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Distribution and ecology. – Lepidocupania samoensis is endemic to the two main islands of Samoa, Savai`i and Upolu, where it grows in primary evergreen forests between 650 to 1350 m (ADEMA, 1991).

children.name: Lepidocupania squamosa  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Lepidocupania squamosa was assigned an IUCN risk of extinction status of “ Endangered ” by JAFFRÉ et al. (1998). Since this assessment was conducted, a large portion of the vegetation on the Tiébaghi massif has been cleared for mining, which has surely led to further population decline (especially concerning since this area contained the largest subpopulation of L. squamosa).

children.name: Lepidocupania subfalcata  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – The holotype of this species was initially identified by Guillaumin as C. sebertii Guillaumin, a name considered a synonym of C. fruticosa (≡ Lepidocupania fruticosa) by ADEMA (1991). Our examination of the available herbarium material suggests that further taxonomic analysis is needed to clarify species delimitations within this group, which probably represents a species complex.

children.name: Lepidocupania tontoutensis  Buerki, Callm., Munzinger & Lowry
children.description: Notes. – Cupaniopsis tontoutensis was described based on Virot 1448. Original material at P is, however, mounted on two sheets, only one of which [P 00639164] bears the name of Guillaumin’s new species in his own hand, along with the word “ type ”. We regard this specimen as the holotype.
